title: Tim Cook Bids Farewell as Apple Posts Record $109.4 Billion Quarter
excerpt: In his final earnings call as CEO, Cook presided over Apple's strongest June quarter ever, with iPhone sales surging 22% and profits beating Wall Street forecasts — but a cautious Q4 outlook sent shares lower after hours.
body:
• Apple reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16.4% year-over-year, beating analyst estimates of $108.65 billion in Tim Cook's final earnings call as CEO.
  • iPhone sales surged 21.7% to $54.3 billion — Apple's best-ever third quarter for the device — while Mac revenue hit a spring-quarter record of $10.4 billion, up 28.7%.
  • Cook will step down on September 1 and become executive chairman; hardware engineering chief John Ternus takes over as Apple's next CEO.
  • Shares fell 3.8% in after-hours trading after Apple guided Q4 revenue growth of 9–11%, missing Wall Street's 12.1% estimate, citing component shortages and FX headwinds.

Tim Cook led Apple's quarterly earnings call for the last time on Thursday evening, delivering record June-quarter results before handing the reins to his successor. The company reported revenue of $109.4 billion for the fiscal third quarter ended June 27, up 16.4% from a year earlier and ahead of the $108.65 billion analysts had expected.

Profit rose 27% year-over-year to $29.8 billion, comfortably beating Wall Street's forecast of $27.8 billion. Tariff refunds added roughly 5% to the quarter's bottom line, and Cook said the company is reinvesting that money into domestic manufacturing as part of Apple's $600 billion, four-year commitment to the U.S. economy.

iPhone Drives a Blockbuster Quarter

iPhone revenue climbed 21.7% to $54.3 billion, above estimates of $53.9 billion and Apple's strongest-ever third quarter for the device. The spike came even as customers typically slow purchases ahead of new fall models. This year, a global memory chip crunch — with prices soaring as much as 600% over two years — has pushed buyers to lock in current pricing before anticipated iPhone price hikes later this year.

Mac revenue jumped 28.7% to $10.4 billion, smashing estimates of $8.7 billion and setting a new spring-quarter record. Cook credited the $699 MacBook Neo as the company's bestselling computer in the U.S. during its first full quarter on the market, while demand for the higher-end Mac Studio created supply shortages.

Not everything landed. iPad sales dropped 5.9% to $6.2 billion, missing the $6.92 billion estimate, which Cook attributed to a "tough compare" against last year's launch of the budget A16 iPad. Services revenue grew 12.1% to $30.7 billion but fell short of the $31.2 billion forecast.

A Cautious Outlook Rattles Investors

Despite the strong quarter, Apple's guidance spooked the market. CFO Kevan Parekh projected fourth-quarter revenue growth of 9% to 11% year-over-year — below the 12.1% analysts had modeled — citing component shortages and foreign exchange pressure. iPhone revenue is expected to grow in the "mid-teens," constrained by ongoing supply chain issues.

Shares dropped 3.8%, or $12.54, to $320.71 in after-hours trading. The stock had entered the call near all-time highs, up roughly 25% year-to-date, and Apple briefly surpassed $5 trillion in market value earlier this week.

"I've had an incredible opportunity to work with people that I love to work with... and it's just been the privilege of a lifetime."

— Tim Cook, outgoing Apple CEO

Cook's Legacy and What Comes Next

Cook will step down as CEO on September 1, transitioning to the role of executive chairman. John Ternus, Apple's senior vice president of hardware engineering who has been with the company since 2013, takes over. Ternus spoke briefly on the April call, but Thursday was largely Cook's farewell.

Cook took over from co-founder Steve Jobs in 2011, when many doubted whether a supply chain expert could maintain Apple's product-driven culture. Fifteen years later, the company's market value has grown more than 1,000% — from under $400 billion to nearly $5 trillion. Revenue during Cook's tenure tripled, and the company created what Barron's estimated at roughly $4 trillion in shareholder value.

"I couldn't be more excited to watch our phenomenal story of innovation continue to unfold, and I've never been more confident that the best is yet to come."

— Tim Cook, on his final earnings call

AI Strategy and China

Cook addressed Apple's approach to artificial intelligence, expressing openness toward open-source AI models. "They are useful," he said, signaling a pragmatic stance as the company prepares to launch its AI-powered Siri overhaul this fall using Google's Gemini. Apple Intelligence has finally received approval in China after a nearly two-year delay, potentially strengthening the company's hand in a market where domestic rivals have moved aggressively on generative AI.

China revenue rose 22% to $18.81 billion during the quarter, though it fell short of the $19.5 billion analysts expected. Cook struck an optimistic tone about U.S.-China relations, citing a state dinner he attended in April.

What's Next

Ternus inherits a company at an inflection point: Apple is the world's most valuable consumer technology franchise, but faces memory cost inflation that could squeeze margins, an AI race where it remains a relative latecomer, and the challenge of sustaining growth at enormous scale. Whether he can match Cook's record — or carve out a distinct chapter — will be Wall Street's next question when Apple reports again in October.
